question: Can short generated videos be evaluated as physical world models by extracting object trajectories and scoring governing equations and conserved quantities instead of matching one reference trajectory or asking a vision-language judge?

key_findings.claim: Morpheus defines physics-conditioned scores over 130 controlled real experiments rather than assuming a unique pixel trajectory.
key_findings.evidence: Recordings cover falling, projectile, pendulum, sliding, collision, rolling, spring, bouncing, and other rigid-body processes with varied initial conditions. Generated object tracks feed per-experiment PINN equation residuals and conservation statistics.

key_findings.claim: All evaluated generators remain far below real-video physics scores, and temporal boundary information is more valuable than model provenance.
key_findings.evidence: Real videos score 0.96-0.99 dynamically and at least 0.90 on invariance with zero discard. The best generated aggregate is 0.66 for Wan2.1 keyframe interpolation with 0.16 discard; Cosmos multi-frame reaches 0.59 versus 0.50 single-frame.

key_findings.claim: A specialized VLM judge fails a basic real-video calibration test.
key_findings.evidence: VideoPhy2-AutoEval gives real recordings physical-commonsense 3.71 versus 3.53 for generations, only 58.5% versus 51.1% rule adherence, and 23.6% real-video joint pass rate, including zero passes for several clean experiment types.

key_findings.claim: The metric correlates with a small human study and is locally robust to injected trajectory noise, but this does not validate unconstrained video.
key_findings.evidence: Across 42 videos and three judges, total score has Spearman correlation 0.708; injected jitter or up to 20% gaps changes scores by at most 3%. The study is restricted to short, stationary-camera, controlled Newtonian scenes.

method.core_idea: Evaluate whether generated motion belongs to the set allowed by known physical laws, rather than whether it reproduces one observed future.
method.mechanism: Condition generators on stylized real frames, segment and track objects, reject disappearance/duplication/stillness, smooth differentiated trajectories, fit per-system physics-informed neural networks, score normalized equation fit, and score temporal variance of invariants such as energy, acceleration, momentum, or period.
assumptions: Two-dimensional tracked centroids retain enough state to identify the tested physical constraints.
Camera scale and hidden physical parameters can be absorbed without invalidating normalized scores.
Discarding untrackable generations is fairly incorporated by assigning minimal physics score.
The hand-specified equations and invariants cover the important failure dimensions.

techniques.role: Scores membership in a physically valid trajectory family rather than distance to one future.
Fits noisy video tracks while penalizing violation of the relevant ODE.
Measures whether experiment-specific invariants remain constant over generated motion.
Requires automatic judges to rate clean real physics near the ceiling.

evaluations.setting: Nine current open and closed video generators over controlled rigid-body experiments
evaluations.metric: Discard rate and mean dynamical/invariance score
evaluations.result: Best generated score 0.66 versus real-video scores near 0.9-1.0
evaluations.baseline: Clean real recordings and alternative conditioning modes

evaluations.setting: VLM automatic judging on real and generated videos
evaluations.metric: Physical commonsense, rule adherence, joint pass
evaluations.result: Only 23.6% of real videos pass jointly versus 13.9% generated

evaluations.setting: 42-video human plausibility sample plus synthetic tracking perturbations
evaluations.metric: Spearman correlation and relative score deviation
evaluations.result: Correlation 0.708; deviation no more than 3% under tested jitter/gaps
evaluations.baseline: Averaged three-judge ratings and unperturbed tracks

limitations: Author-stated: evaluation is limited to Newtonian rigid bodies in short videos without camera motion.
Reviewer-identified: 2D centroids omit rotation, depth, deformation, contact forces, and hidden masses that can determine physical validity.
Reviewer-identified: filtering plus zero-scoring conflates generator physics failure with detector/tracker failure.
Reviewer-identified: human validation uses only 42 videos and three judges.
Reviewer-identified: hand-selected law families do not show that the generator has a reusable internal world model.
failure_modes: A visually wrong video can satisfy a low-dimensional invariant by coincidence.
Smoothing can remove high-frequency violations or create apparent conservation.
Unknown camera motion or perspective changes can masquerade as acceleration.
A generator can exploit keyframe interpolation without learning extrapolative dynamics.
reusable_insights: Validate automatic evaluators on unquestioned real positive controls.
Use a set-valued physical criterion when many futures are valid.
Report untrackable-output rate beside conditional-on-success physics scores.
open_questions: Can law-based scoring extend to 3D articulated, contact-rich, deformable, and camera-moving scenes?
Do higher Morpheus scores predict usefulness for planning or control?
Can generators be trained directly against differentiable law residuals without metric gaming?

competitive_landscape.title: How Far is Video Generation from World Model: A Physical Law Perspective
competitive_landscape.difference: PhyWorld trains video diffusion on deterministic 2D simulations and tests in-/out-of-distribution rule generalization; Morpheus evaluates off-the-shelf models on real controlled experiments with equation and invariant scores.

competitive_landscape.title: VideoPhy: Evaluating Physical Commonsense for Video Generation
competitive_landscape.difference: VideoPhy uses curated text prompts, human labels, and a learned VLM evaluator across diverse materials; Morpheus narrows to measurable Newtonian systems and replaces categorical judgment with explicit laws.

competitive_landscape.title: VideoPhy-2: A Challenging Action-Centric Physical Commonsense Evaluation in Video Generation
competitive_landscape.difference: VideoPhy-2 expands action-centric human and VLM rule evaluation; Morpheus demonstrates that its AutoEval is poorly calibrated on clean real recordings and argues for physics-informed metrics.

novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference: Morpheus's strongest novelty is a real-video positive-control benchmark with explicit ODE and conservation scoring that exposes both generator and VLM-judge failures. Physical-law video benchmarks already exist, and the narrow controlled setup cannot justify broad world-model claims.
reviewer_notes: Read the full main paper and relevant validation/limitation text in the 2026 revision. Current competing arXiv records were checked on 2026-08-23.
